question: A 25-year-old woman admitted to the hospital for the treatment of thyrotoxicosis suddenly becomes severely dyspneic. Her vitals are as follows: blood pressure 60/40 mm Hg, heart rate 180/minute with irregularly regular pulse, and cold peripheries. ECG reveals fast atrial fibrillation; her ECG done one day earlier had only revealed tachycardia. Chest x-ray reveals frank pulmonary edema. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?
Which one of the following is an important step in the management of heat stroke?

answers.option: Rapid cooling of body temperature by spraying with water and cooling
Application of ice packs in the axilla and groin
Intravenous fluid replacement with cold crystalloid solution

question: Defective absorption of which of the following micronutrients is associated with acrodermatitis enteropathica?

A young male was brought to the emergency room after ingestion of 50 tablets of aspirin six hours ago. On examination, the patient appeared agitated and confused. Plasma salicylate levels were 600 mg/L. What is the best way to remove the poison from the body at this stage?
Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment for ischemic stroke during the first three hours?

answers.option: Intravenous thrombolysis using activated tissue plasminogen activator (TPA)

question: A 50-year-old patient presents to the clinic with complaints of lancinating pain in his lower limbs. He further reveals that the pain is mainly felt on the anterior aspect of the legs and the pain is exaggerated at night. His past medical history is significant for diabetes mellitus which was diagnosed 20 years ago. A lower limb examination reveals absent tendon reflexes in both the lower limbs. Which of the following is the likely diagnosis?
Which of the following is the recommended empirical therapy for adult patients presenting with pyogenic meningitis without a rash?
What is the first-line antiepileptic drug for immediate control of generalized tonic-clonic seizures?

A patient with a known case of congestive heart failure, and also taking medications for some sort of arthritis, presents to the emergency department with increased shortness of breath. Which of the following drugs is responsible for this?

A male came to the outpatient department with the complaints of epistaxis and mucosal bleeding. Bleeding time is more than 5 minutes. Factor VIII and VIIIC are reduced. There is a history of similar illness in the family. What is your diagnosis?
Hypertriglyceridemia is associated with which of the following condition?

A 74-year-old man with bipolar I disorder, hypertension, and type-2 diabetes mellitus, who is confused and irritable is brought to the clinic by his son. The patient has a 2-day history of severe vomiting and diarrhea. On examination, he has bilateral tremors of the hand. He is diagnosed with lithium toxicity. 
What is the first line of treatment for lithium toxicity?

answers.option: Whole bowel irrigation with polyethylene glycol (PEG)

question:
A 34-year-old woman presents to the outpatient department for a check-up 1 year after she had been prescribed fenofibrate for a medical condition that causes deranged lipid profiles. She tells you that she often forgets to take her medication. 

Furthermore, she tells you that her maternal uncles have deranged lipid profiles for which they take medications. 

On physical examination, her height is 5'4" (163 cm), weight is 82 kg (180 pounds) and BMI is 31.6. She has bilateral yellow plaques on her eyelids and nodular, firm, painless swellings on the extensor surfaces of her hands. 

Laboratory studies are significant for triglycerides = 1100 mg/dL (12.43 mmol/L).

Which of the following conditions is this patient most likely at risk of developing?

A young female presents to the clinic with complaints of exertional dyspnea, fatigue, and diarrhea. Stool examination shows the presence of proglottids. CBC shows Hb = 8 g/dL, MCV = 110, presence of hyper-segmented neutrophils and eosinophilia. The physician is suspecting a worm infection. 
Which of the following species is this patient most likely infected by?

A 30-year-old man presents with a history of hematuria for 15 days. He also had an episode of gum bleed one day back. Considering idiopathic thrombocytopenic purpura (ITP) as the diagnosis, which of the following is the best initial treatment of choice?
A patient who is taking antithyroid drugs for hyperthyroidism develops sore throat and fever. Her total leukocyte count is low. Which of the following drugs is she most likely taking?

A 34-year-old intravenous drug abuser presents to the emergency room with complaints of severe right hypochondrial pain and high-grade fever for 3 days. On examination, he is icteric, mildly anemic, and has tender hepatomegaly and a dull percussion note on the right lower chest. His initial investigations reveal hemoglobin 11.2 gm/dl, ALT 64 IU, AST 60 IU, ALP 184, gamma-GT 84 IU, and total leukocyte count 14,200/uL (neutrophils 80%). Ultrasound abdomen shows a rounded opacity of 8.4 cm in the right lobe of the liver. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 60-year-old female presents to the clinic with complaints of pins and needles sensation along with burning feet over the last 8 to 9 months. She is a known case of diabetes and has been non-compliant with oral hypoglycemic therapy for the last 15 years. Clinical examination reveals sensory loss in a stocking pattern, absent ankle jerks, and subtle weakness of dorsiflexion of the toes. Which of the following is the dominant type of neuropathy in this patient?

A 62-year-old male admitted to the hospital is being evaluated for vomiting and frank blood in the urine. One day prior to his admission he was involved in a road traffic accident. On the third day of admission, he became oliguric. His investigations today are the following: hemoglobin 10.1 gm/dl, urea 218 mg/dl, creatinine 7.8 mg/dl, and potassium 6.8 mEq/L. Which of the following is the best immediate treatment?

A 50-year-old female who has recently been diagnosed with hypertension presents to the clinic for a routine follow-up examination. On workup, she has abnormal values of hemoglobin (Hb) 7.4 mg/dl, MCV 84 fl, creatinine 5.4 mg/dl, blood urea nitrogen (BUN) 65 mmol/L, potassium 5.2 mEq/L, sodium 130 mEq/L, phosphorus 5.0 mEq/L, calcium 6.7 mg/dl. Which of the following is the most likely cause of decreased Hb in this patient?

A 16-year-old boy presents to the emergency department with the complaint of swelling of the right knee joint after trivial trauma. History is significant for similar incidences over the past 4 years. Their family history is positive for a bleeding disorder. Investigations show: hemoglobin -  10 g/dL, white cell count - 5,000/uL, platelets - 200,000/uL, factor VIII - normal, prothrombin time (PT) - 16 seconds (control - 14 seconds), activated partial thromboplastin time (APTT) - 48 seconds (control - 35 seconds). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

An 8-year-old boy presents to the emergency department with complaints of abdominal pain and distension. He is pale and malnourished; you suspect he has a worm infestation. Which of the following organism is most likely the cause of intestinal obstruction as a complication?
Which one of these disorders are characterized by the presence of 'smudge cells' in the peripheral smear?

A 25-year-old female presents to the neurology clinic with sudden onset of bilateral visual loss and severe back pain. She reports no prior history of neurological or ophthalmological problems and no other significant medical history. Examination reveals bilateral optic neuritis and spinal MRI reveals inflammation along segments C4-C8. What is the investigation of choice?
Which of these drugs is notorious for causing 'agranulocytosis'?

A 55-year-old man presents to the clinic with complaints of weakness in his arms for the past 6 months. He reports that the weakness has been gradually progressing and is now affecting his ability to perform daily activities such as dressing and writing. He also noticed stiffness in his legs at this time. Neurological examination reveals hyperreflexia, spasticity, and a positive Babinski sign in both lower limbs, and fasciculations in the upper limbs. What is the most likely diagnosis?
Which one of these is the investigation of choice for Guillain Barre syndrome?

A 14-year-old girl comes to the clinic complaining of primary amenorrhea. She has never had her menstrual period and is concerned about it. During the examination, the pediatrician notes that the girl is shorter than her peers and has a webbed neck and low-set ears. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 24 year-old-male comes to the office due to numbness on the dorsal aspect of the lateral three-and-a-half fingers, and weakness of extension at the wrist and fingers after receiving an intramuscular injection on his shoulder. 

Which of the following nerves is most likely damaged?

A 16-year-old boy is brought to the clinic with generalized weakness and easy bruising. His complete blood profile shows pancytopenia. Peripheral film shows giant metamyelocytes with large sausage-shaped nuclei. His bilirubin is  3 mg%. The reticulocyte count is 0.5%. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
Occurrence of one or more depressive episodes with hypomania is seen in which of the following?
Which of the following is the most common site for extrapulmonary tuberculosis?
Which of the following is the treatment of choice for severe falciparum malaria?
Which of the following is the investigation of choice for multiple sclerosis?

A 40-year-old male patient presents to the clinic with complaints of difficulty in voiding urine. He also complains of lower back pain. On general physical examination, signs of anemia are positive. Which of the following investigations is best suited to help with the diagnosis?

A lady came to the outpatient department complaining of proximal muscle weakness. She has difficulty in climbing and combing her hair. On examination, she held the doctor's hand and could not release it. What is your diagnosis?
A patient is suspected of having Cushing's disease. Which one of the following lab investigations should be ordered as the next step in management to confirm the diagnosis?

answers.option: Measurement of cyclicity of cortisol secretion

question: Which of the following are the earliest changes pathological changes seen in diabetic nephropathy?
Which of the following drugs can be used to treat genital herpes simplex?

A 60-year-old female presents with fatigue, easy bruising, and recurrent infections. Laboratory reports indicate pancytopenia, with low hemoglobin, reduced platelet count, and decreased white blood cell count. A bone marrow biopsy confirms the diagnosis of aplastic anemia. What is the recommended treatment for this patient's condition based on the clinical and laboratory findings?
What is the most common causative organism for the traveler's diarrhea in developing countries?
Which of the following is incorrect regarding leptospirosis?

answers.option: PCR detects DNA of organism in both blood and urine
Illness is seen in sewage workers
Initial disease presentation includes fever, myalgia, and conjunctival congestion
Infection is transmitted by rodents through urine
Diagnosis requires neutrophil leucocytosis, abnormal LFTs, and presence of albumin and casts in urine

question: A 66-year-old male presents to the clinic with the complaint of painful asymmetrical quadriceps muscle wasting. He is a known case of diabetes for the last 10 years. Clinical examination reveals an absent knee reflex on the affected side. What is the type of neuropathy in this patient?

A 65-year-old female presented to the clinic with an altered level of consciousness.  She is a known case of type 2 diabetes mellitus. On examination, the patient appears severely dehydrated. Her biochemical profile reveals a random blood sugar of 652 mg/dl, ph of 7.35, Na+ of 155 mmol/L, K+ of 5 mmol/L, Cl- of 110 mmol/L, and HCO3 of 30 mmol/L. What will be the first step in the management of this patient?
Which of the following is the best treatment option for pseudotumor cerebri at the time of its initial diagnosis?
Which of the following laboratory tests can be used to differentiate acute renal failure from chronic renal failure?

A 21-year-old obese female presented to the clinic with the complaint of frequent headaches and blurring of vision for the last six months. She has had a history of irregular periods for the last three years. Neurological examination reveals six cranial nerve palsy. The rest of the systemic examination is normal. Fundoscopy shows bilateral papilledema. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 20-year-old female presents to the clinic with the complaint of recurrent hypoglycemic attacks. During one such attack, she had glucose levels of 45 mg/dl, high insulin levels, and low C-peptide levels. What is the most likely cause of these hypoglycemic attacks?
A 60-year-old male presents to the clinic with the complaints of lower urinary tract symptoms, backache, weight loss, and anemia. Which of the following tests is diagnostically important?
What is the most common complication of peritoneal dialysis?
Which one of the following conditions has elevated thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH) receptor antibodies in 80 to 95% of the patients?
Which of the following statements is correct about the epidemiology of diabetes mellitus?

answers.option: Diabetes mellitus is more common in Britain than the Indian subcontinent
Incidence of type 2 diabetes is rising
Incidences of both type 1 and type 2 diabetes are rising
Type 1 diabetes is more common than type two diabetes
Type 2 diabetes is more common in Caucasian population

question: Which of the following is the best way to diagnose Parkinson‘s disease?
Which one of the following conditions has high luteinizing hormone, progesterone, and testosterone levels with normal estradiol levels?
Which one of the following steps is not required during the management of major bleeding secondary to the excessive anticoagulant effect of oral anticoagulants?

answers.option: Transfuse whole blood in severe anemia

question: Which one of the following conditions does not cause hyper-gonadotrophic hypogonadism?
Which of the following is the best investigation for the diagnosis of delayed puberty and hypogonadism?

answers.option: Luteinizing hormone (LH) and follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) in boys
Chromosome analysis is performed if gonadotrophin concentrations are depressed
Empirical treatment with testosterone followed by measurement of follicle-stimulating hormone and luteinizing hormone in males
Chromosome analysis is performed if gonadotrophin concentrations are elevated
Luteinizing hormone, follicle-stimulating hormone, testosterone, and estradiol levels in girls

question: Enhanced hydration is used in patients receiving chemotherapy for cancer to prevent which of the following conditions?
Which of the following statements is correct regarding renal cell carcinoma?

answers.option: There is an early invasion of the renal cortex
Glomerular cell tumors are more common
Hematogenous metastasis occurs to para-aortic lymph nodes

question: An old man is brought to the emergency department after he falls down and becomes drowsy while working in the garden in very hot weather. He is initially oliguric, and eventually becomes anuric. What is the most likely diagnosis?
Which one of the following statements about short stature is incorrect?

answers.option: Children with constitutional short stature have a normal growth velocity and normal bone age
Intrauterine growth retardation results in short stature
Malabsorption should be ruled out in every patient

question: Which one of the following is the most important step in the immediate management of high-altitude cerebral edema?

answers.option: Oxygen therapy through a pressurized portable bag

question: What is the management of moderate aspirin poisoning?

answers.option: A single dose of activated charcoal

question: A person is sitting alone and talking to himself. What is he most likely experiencing?
Which one of the following statements about motor neuron disease is false?

answers.option: The presence of brisk reflexes, and fasciculations in wasted limbs without sensory involvement is typical
About 10% of cases are familial, showing autosomal dominant inheritance
The incidence of the disease is about 5–10/100,000
Cerebrospinal fluid examination shows a slight elevation of protein
In amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, there is early involvement of the tongue, palate, and pharyngeal muscles, with predominant pyramidal tract features

question: Pseudo-hyponatremia is a feature of which one of the following conditions?
What is most important for the assessment of renal osteodystrophy in chronic renal failure?

answers.option: Serum calcium, phosphate, and parathyroid hormone

question: A 12-year-old young boy presented to the clinic with the complaint of severe loin pain. Laboratory investigations reveal serum K+ of 2.5 mmol, urinary ph of 6.5, and normal urea levels. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 67-year-old male presents to the clinic with the complaint of paresthesia of the hands and feet. He has a long-standing history of alcoholism. He has also been on anti-tuberculous therapy for the last 4 months. What is the most likely cause of his presentation?
Which one of the following is the main differentiating feature between pre-renal failure and acute tubular necrosis?

answers.option: Urea and creatinine are increased in pre-renal failure
Urine osmolarity is less than 350 mOsm/kg in acute tubular necrosis
Urinary sodium levels are less than 20 mmol/L in pre-renal failure
There is dilute urine in acute tubular necrosis
Plasma osmolality is increased in pre-renal failure

question: What is the most common cause of erectile dysfunction?

An 80-year-old male presented to the clinic with the complaint of bilateral hand tremors, rigidity, and slowness of movements. Clinical examination reveals bilateral brisk knee-jerk reflexes and upward plantars. What is the most likely diagnosis?

answers.option: Subacute, combined degeneration of the cord

question: What is the definitive treatment for a patient under 40 years of age presenting with Graves’ disease?

answers.option: High dose anti-thyroid drugs with thyroxine supplementation

question: A 60-year-old male presented to the clinic with the complaint of generalized joint stiffness with increased difficulty in walking, getting out of bed, shaving, and writing. He also complains of rest tremors in his right hand. According to his wife, he has become progressively less active and more expressionless, despite being on antidepressant therapy for the last three months. What is the most likely diagnosis?
Which of the following statements about metabolic acidosis is correct?

answers.option: Serum bicarbonate levels are less than 24 mmol/L
Blood H+ is less than 40 nmol/liter

question: A 27-year-old female develops acute meningococcal meningitis. Which of the following drugs should be given for prophylaxis to her 32-year-old husband and a three-year-old son?
Which of the following treatments has not been proven to be successful for the prevention of stroke?

answers.option: Carotid endarterectomy in 70% or more of ipsilateral stenosis

question: Which of the following statements is true about schizophrenia?

answers.option: It may be precipitated by social stress
Recent evidence suggests it’s a functional disorder
There is no neurodevelopmental abnormality detected
There is no role of genes

question: Which one of the following statements about myasthenia gravis is incorrect?

answers.option: Muscle fatiguability is a cardinal symptom
Myasthenia gravis has no association with other autoimmune diseases
Tensilon test is an easy diagnostic test
Intravenous immunoglobulin administration is an alternative to plasma exchange for the management of myasthenia gravis
Acetylcholine receptor auto-antibodies are detected in the serum

question: Which one of the following is the most accurate statement regarding diabetes insipidus?

answers.option: The diagnosis is confirmed by plasma osmolality of more than 300 mOsm/kg and urine osmolality of less than 600 mOsm/kg
Primary polydipsia has low plasma osmolality

question: What is the best screening test for Cushing's syndrome?
Which one of the following conditions is not characterized by gynecomastia secondary to hormonal changes?

answers.option: Human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG)-secreting tumor of the lungs

question: A 70-year-old female presents to the clinic complaining of progressive memory loss and episodes of abnormal behavior with disorientation. There is no past history of falls or any systemic disorder. What is the best initial step for the diagnosis of her neurological state?

answers.option: Blood tests to exclude metabolic causes
CT scan of the brain to exclude subdural hemorrhage
Clinical examination and cognitive testing to diagnose dementia

question: A 40-year-old patient presents to the clinic with the complaint of severe bone pain. She is a known case of chronic renal failure and is not on dialysis. Her laboratory investigations reveal urea of 100 mg/dl, serum creatinine of 5 mg/dl, serum calcium of 12 mg/dl, serum phosphate of 3.8 mg/dl, and raised alkaline phosphate levels. Bone X-ray reveals bone cysts. What is the most likely cause of this metabolic bone disease?
Which one of the following statements about membranous nephropathy is the most accurate?

answers.option: It may present with asymptomatic proteinuria
Young males have a better prognosis
Less than 50% of patients may undergo spontaneous remission
Frank nephrotic syndrome is very unlikely
It is the most common cause of nephrotic syndrome in females

question: A 44-year-old male is referred to the hypertension clinic for evaluation of blood pressure that has remained 165/100 mmHg despite being on three antihypertensive medications. Laboratory studies reveal a serum potassium of 3.1 mEq/L (Hypokalemia), a serum sodium of 146 mEq/L (Hypernatremia), and a significantly elevated Plasma Aldosterone Concentration (PAC) with a suppressed Plasma Renin Activity (PRA) (PAC/PRA ratio >30). After a salt-loading suppression test confirms the diagnosis of Primary Hyperaldosteronism, what is the most appropriate next step in the diagnostic evaluation?

A 16-year-old boy presents with a 3-year history of persistent fatigue, polyuria, and generalized muscle weakness, with a motor examination revealing 2/5 strength. Physical examination shows a blood pressure of 100/60 mmHg. Laboratory investigations are significant for a serum sodium of 138 mEq/L, a profoundly low potassium of 2.5 mEq/L, and a chloride of 100 mEq/L. Arterial blood gas analysis shows a bicarbonate level of 30 mEq/L, indicating a metabolic alkalosis. Given the patient’s age of onset, the presence of normotension, and the specific electrolyte pattern, which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 35-year-old patient presents with classic cushingoid features, including a "buffalo hump," abdominal striae, and central obesity. Initial screening reveals an elevated 24-hour urinary free cortisol level. To confirm the diagnosis of Cushing syndrome and rule out pseudo-Cushing states, which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

A 24-year-old male is brought to the emergency department 30 minutes after being bitten by a snake while hiking. On arrival, he is hemodynamically stable, but physical examination reveals two clear fang marks on his right ankle with rapidly progressing local edema and ecchymosis. Laboratory studies are significant for a falling fibrinogen level and the presence of gross hematuria. Which of the following findings is a definitive indication for the administration of antivenom?

A 60-year-old male painter with a long history of diabetes presents with progressive bilateral wrist weakness, recurrent episodes of poorly localized abdominal pain, and a history of seizures. Physical examination reveals bilateral wrist drop and a thin blue line along the gingival margin. Laboratory investigations are significant for a microcytic anemia with prominent basophilic stippling on the peripheral blood smear. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 17-year-old female presents with persistent gum bleeding following a routine tooth extraction. She reports no previous history of significant mucosal bleeding or easy bruising, although she mentions her brother has experienced similar episodes after minor procedures. Physical examination is unremarkable. Laboratory investigations reveal a platelet count of 164,000/µL, a bleeding time of 5 minutes, and a hemoglobin of 13.1 g/dL. All other coagulation studies, including PT and aPTT, are within the normal reference range. Given the family history and the mild clinical presentation triggered only by surgical stress, which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 72-year-old male with a history of heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) and atrial fibrillation is being started on Digoxin for rate control. While discussing the potential risks and clinical applications of the drug, which of the following statements regarding Digoxin is true?

answers.option: Can increase conduction through an accessory pathway
Safe for use in patients with end-stage renal failure
Used for the treatment of ventricular tachycardia

question: A 64-year-old male with a long-standing history of persistent asthma and Congestive Heart Failure (CHF) with an ejection fraction of 35% presents to the clinic for a follow-up. He reports occasional shortness of breath and palpitations. On examination, he has mild bilateral pedal edema and scattered expiratory wheezes. You are reviewing his medication list to optimize his respiratory symptoms while minimizing cardiac strain. Which of the following classes of asthma medications should be used with extreme caution or avoided if possible in this patient due to its potential to exacerbate his underlying cardiac condition?

A 48-year-old male with a history of resistant hypertension presents with persistent fatigue and muscle cramps. Laboratory investigations reveal a serum potassium of 3.0 mEq/L and a bicarbonate level of 32 mEq/L. Further hormonal assay confirms Primary Hyperaldosteronism with a significantly elevated plasma aldosterone concentration (PAC) and a suppressed plasma renin activity (PRA). After confirming the diagnosis with a salt-loading suppression test, what is the most appropriate next step to determine the etiology of the aldosterone excess?

A 45-year-old female presents with clinical features of hypothyroidism, including fatigue, cold intolerance, and weight gain. Physical examination is significant for a diffuse, non-tender goiter. Laboratory investigations reveal a low Thyroid Stimulating Hormone (TSH) and a low free thyroxine (T4), confirming a diagnosis of primary hypothyroidism. Which of the following antibodies is most characteristically associated with this patient's condition?

A 68-year-old patient with a long-standing history of hypertension and diabetes is found to have a serum creatinine of 3.2 mg/dL. Calculations reveal a Glomerular Filtration Rate (eGFR) of 18 mL/min/1.73m². The patient has had similar laboratory values for the past four months. Based on the Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) classification, which stage of Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) does this patient's renal function represent?

A 17-year-old male presents for a medical evaluation due to persistent short stature and delayed puberty. Physical examination reveals a height significantly below the 3rd percentile for his age and sex, with a lack of secondary sexual characteristics (Tanner Stage 1). Laboratory investigations show a profoundly low Insulin-like Growth Factor 1 (IGF-1) level. Given the clinical presentation and laboratory findings, which of the following is the most likely underlying diagnosis?

answers.option: Constitutional delay of growth and puberty

question: A 28-year-old patient presents with a 3-day history of progressive weakness in both the upper and lower limbs. Physical examination confirms motor weakness, but Notably, there is no sensory loss and no urinary incontinence. The patient’s surgical history is significant for three previous exploratory laparotomies due to unexplained, severe abdominal pain. Additionally, she reports a history of two generalized seizures approximately 10 years ago. Given the combination of acute neurological symptoms and a history of recurrent, "surgical-mimic" abdominal pain, which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 65-year-old male with a long-standing history of diabetes presents with a 4-month history of progressive numbness and a "pins and needles" sensation in his hands and feet. His family reports increasing forgetfulness and irritability over the same period. The patient has worked as a professional painter for over 30 years, specializing in the restoration of older homes. Physical examination reveals decreased distal sensation and mild cognitive impairment. Laboratory investigations are significant for a microcytic anemia with basophilic stippling and a mildly raised ALT. Given his occupational history and the combination of neurological and hepatic findings, which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 62-year-old patient with a long-standing history of hypertension and generalized atherosclerosis is started on an ACE inhibitor (Enalapril) to manage his blood pressure and provide renal protection. One week later, follow-up laboratory investigations reveal a significant increase in serum creatinine from 1.2 mg/dL to 2.1 mg/dL (>30% increase). The patient remains asymptomatic, and his physical examination is unremarkable except for bilateral abdominal bruits. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this acute decline in renal function?

A 60-year-old male is brought to the clinic by his family due to a 2-year history of progressive forgetfulness, including difficulty recognizing close family members. On one occasion, he was found wandering in his garden by a policeman, unable to find his way back to his house. His family reports that he frequently talks to himself and claims he can talk to his dead relatives. Additionally, he exhibits significant mood swings, alternating between periods of intense irritability and sudden crying spells. Physical examination is unremarkable for focal neurological deficits. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 22-year-old student presents to the student health clinic reporting a one-year history of persistent low mood and a significant lack of interest in his medical studies. He describes sleeping up to 12 hours a day (hypersomnolence) and having an insatiable appetite (hyperphagia), leading to a 15-pound weight gain. He notes that his mood occasionally brightens briefly when he receives a good grade or spends time with friends, but he quickly reverts to a state of low energy and "leaden paralysis" in his limbs. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 29-year-old agricultural worker presents with an itchy, "serpiginous" red rash on his buttocks that seems to move rapidly over several hours (larva currens). He also reports intermittent abdominal pain and loose stools. Stool microscopy reveals rhabditiform larvae. Which of the following is the most appropriate first-line treatment for this infection?

A 26-year-old male is brought to the emergency department by his friends after being found unresponsive in a park. On examination, he is stuporous with a respiratory rate of 6 breaths per minute. Physical examination reveals pinpoint pupils (miosis) and evidence of urinary incontinence. There are visible track marks on his forearms. Oxygen saturation is 84% on room air. What is the most appropriate initial pharmacological intervention for this patient?

A 28-year-old male presents with a one-week history of high-grade fever, chills, and a dry cough. Physical examination reveals a significant fever (102°F) and hepatosplenomegaly. Laboratory findings are notable for leukopenia (TLC 2,300/μL) and a mild elevation in ALT, while hemoglobin and platelets remain within normal limits. Given the prolonged fever, systemic involvement (organomegaly), and classic hematologic picture, which of the following is the most appropriate next step before initiating treatment?

answers.option: Immunochromatographic test for malarial parasite (ICT MP)

question: A 24-year-old male presents for a follow-up of unintended weight loss and persistent thirst. He reports losing 7 kg over the past two months despite an increased appetite. Laboratory investigations reveal an HbA1c of 11%, a fasting plasma glucose of 280 mg/dL, and a random glucose of 345 mg/dL. Urinalysis is positive for glucose but negative for ketones. Given the severe hyperglycemia, symptomatic weight loss, and markedly elevated HbA1c, what is the most appropriate initial treatment strategy?

answers.option: Lifestyle modifications and reassess in 3 months

question: A 2-week-old infant is brought to the pediatrician due to persistent jaundice, vomiting, and poor weight gain since birth. Physical examination reveals hepatomegaly and early lens opacities (cataracts). Laboratory tests show aminoaciduria and a positive substances-reducing test in the urine, but a negative glucose oxidase test. The parents mention the symptoms worsen after breastfeeding. Galactosemia is suspected, which is a disorder caused by the body's inability to properly metabolize which of the following?

A 52-year-old female with a BMI of 32 kg/m2 is recently diagnosed with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus. Her HbA1c is 7.4%. You decide to initiate Metformin as first-line therapy. During your clinical discussion regarding the drug's pharmacology, which of the following statements is true regarding metformin?

answers.option: Metabolism by liver and kidney both
Increased insulin sensitivity leading to increased hepatic and peripheral fat synthesis

question: A 32-year-old man with a known history of human immunodeficiency virus infection presents to the clinic for a routine health maintenance visit. His most recent laboratory results show a CD4+ T-lymphocyte count of 150/mm³. He is currently adherent to his antiretroviral therapy. He plans to travel to an area where yellow fever and hepatitis B are endemic. Which of the following describes the most appropriate recommendation regarding vaccinations for this patient?

answers.option: Dengue vaccine is recommended as a routine primary series
Live attenuated vaccines should be administered when the CD4+ count is below 200/mm³
Yellow fever vaccine should be administered regardless of CD4+ count
Hepatitis B vaccine is contraindicated in this patient
Inactivated vaccines are generally safe regardless of CD4+ count

question: A 28-year-old woman with human immunodeficiency virus infection presents to the infectious disease clinic for a follow-up appointment. Her last CD4+ T-lymphocyte count was 350/mm³. A tuberculin skin test is performed, which reveals an induration of 8 mm after 48 hours. The patient has no cough, fever, or weight loss, and a chest radiograph shows no active pulmonary infiltrates or hilar lymphadenopathy. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in the management of this patient?

answers.option: Observation and repeat testing in six months
Daily rifampin and pyrazinamide for two months

question: A 29-year-old woman presents to the clinic with a six-month history of milky nipple discharge and the absence of menstrual cycles. She denies any visual field changes or headaches. Physical examination confirms bilateral galactorrhea. Laboratory evaluation reveals a serum prolactin level of 280 ng/mL (normal range is less than 25 ng/mL). A magnetic resonance imaging scan of the brain shows a 6-millimeter well-circumscribed lesion within the anterior pituitary gland. Which of the following is the most appropriate first-line treatment for this patient?

answers.option: Observation with repeat imaging in six months

question: A 7-year-old boy presents to the pediatric clinic with generalized fatigue, pale conjunctivae, and a sore, smooth tongue. His parents report that his diet is well-balanced, but they recently returned from a trip to a region where raw freshwater fish is a dietary staple. Laboratory studies reveal a hemoglobin level of 9.2 g/dL and a mean corpuscular volume of 110 fL. A peripheral blood smear shows macro-ovalocytes and hypersegmented neutrophils. Which of the following parasites is the most likely cause of these findings?

A 4-year-old boy is brought to the pediatric clinic for an evaluation of poor growth and frequent urination. Laboratory studies reveal a normal serum glucose level but significant glucosuria. Further urinalysis demonstrates the presence of multiple amino acids, biphosphate, and low-molecular-weight proteins. Venous blood gas analysis shows a normal anion gap metabolic acidosis. Which of the following conditions is the most likely cause of these findings?

A 58-year-old man with a 10-year history of type 2 diabetes mellitus and chronic heart failure presents for a follow-up appointment. His current hemoglobin A1c is 8.2%. To provide both glycemic control and cardiovascular benefit, the physician initiates a medication that promotes glycosuria. This drug exerts its primary effect by inhibiting the reabsorption of glucose at a specific site within the nephron. Which of the following is the primary site of action for this class of medications?

answers.option: Descending limb of the loop of Henle
Ascending limb of the loop of Henle

question: A 64-year-old man with a history of chronic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction is admitted to the hospital for an exacerbation characterized by increased peripheral edema and dyspnea on exertion. He is started on a high-dose intravenous infusion of furosemide. After three days of therapy, his symptoms have significantly improved, but he reports new-onset generalized muscle weakness and palpitations. An electrocardiogram reveals flattened T waves and the presence of U waves. Which of the following is the most common electrolyte complication associated with this medication?

A 25-year-old man presents to the emergency department with a one-week history of high-grade fever, chills, and rigors. On physical examination, his temperature is 104°F (40°C), pulse is 100/min, and blood pressure is 100/60 mm Hg. The patient reports a significant decrease in urine output over the past three days. Laboratory evaluation reveals a parasite density of 5% on a peripheral blood smear with ring-form trophozoites. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 42-year-old woman undergoes transsphenoidal resection of a non-functioning pituitary macroadenoma. On the second postoperative day, she reports profound fatigue and lightheadedness. Physical examination reveals a blood pressure of 90/60 mm Hg. Laboratory studies show a low serum cortisol, low free thyroxine, and low follicle-stimulating hormone levels. Which of the following is the most likely cause of these findings?

answers.option: Syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone secretion

question: A 34-year-old woman presents with intermittent double vision and drooping of her eyelids that worsens toward the end of the day. She also notes difficulty chewing tough foods. Physical examination reveals bilateral ptosis that improves after the application of an ice pack to the eyes for two minutes. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial diagnostic test for this patient?

An 18-year-old man is brought to the clinic for a progressive gait disturbance. He is now primarily bound to a wheelchair. Physical examination reveals dysarthria, loss of vibratory sense, and absent deep tendon reflexes in the lower extremities. His parents and two siblings are healthy with no similar symptoms. Genetic testing reveals a GAA trinucleotide repeat expansion. Which of the following additional findings is most commonly associated with this condition?

A 22-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department due to a sudden onset of shortness of breath and tingling in her fingertips following a stressful event. Her respiratory rate is 28/min. An arterial blood gas analysis is performed within minutes of symptom onset. Which of the following sets of values is most consistent with an uncompensated respiratory alkalosis?

A 25-year-old man with a history of Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome presents with palpitations. An electrocardiogram reveals atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response and widened QRS complexes. Digoxin is mistakenly administered. The patient's condition rapidly deteriorates into ventricular fibrillation. This occurred because digoxin has which of the following effects in this patient?

answers.option: Increases conduction through the accessory pathway
Increases the refractory period of the atrioventricular node
Decreases the automaticity of the sinoatrial node
Inhibits the sodium-potassium adenosine triphosphatase pump
Decreases conduction through the accessory pathway

question: A 55-year-old man presents with a two-month history of numbness and tingling in his feet. Physical examination shows decreased sensation to pinprick in a stocking-like distribution. To differentiate between a primary demyelinating process and an axonal process, which of the following is the most appropriate diagnostic modality?

answers.option: Skin biopsy for small fiber density
Magnetic resonance imaging of the spine

question: A 30-year-old wildlife handler is bitten by a cobra (Naja naja). Shortly after the incident, he develops blurred vision, difficulty swallowing, and generalized muscle weakness. Physical examination reveals bilateral ptosis and restricted extraocular movements. Which of the following mechanisms best explains the visual problems and paralysis in this patient?

answers.option: Inhibition of calcium release from the sarcoplasmic reticulum
Competitive antagonism of nicotinic acetylcholine receptors

question: A 24-year-old woman presents with a scattered petechial rash on her lower extremities and easy bruising for one week. She denies joint pain, fever, or recent viral illness. Physical examination is unremarkable except for the skin findings; there is no splenomegaly. Laboratory studies show a platelet count of 12,000/mm³, a hemoglobin level of 13.5 g/dL, and a white blood cell count of 7,000/mm³. A peripheral blood smear shows a few large platelets but is otherwise normal. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 38-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department with confusion and a fever of 101.5°F. Laboratory evaluation reveals a hemoglobin level of 8.0 g/dL, a platelet count of 20,000/mm³, and an elevated indirect bilirubin level. A peripheral blood smear shows numerous schistocytes. Her creatinine level is 1.8 mg/dL. Coagulation studies, including prothrombin time and partial thromboplastin time, are within normal limits. Which of the following is the most likely underlying mechanism of this condition?

answers.option: Autoimmune destruction of red blood cells
Sequestration of platelets in the spleen

question: A 45-year-old man presents with progressive weakness in both legs that began two days ago. He notes that the weakness is now involving his hands. He mentions having a diarrheal illness three weeks ago. Physical examination reveals symmetric 2/5 strength in the lower extremities and 4/5 strength in the upper extremities. Deep tendon reflexes are absent at the knees and ankles. Which of the following is the most likely finding on cerebrospinal fluid analysis?

answers.option: Low glucose and elevated white blood cell count
Normal white blood cell count and normal protein
Elevated white blood cell count with normal protein
Elevated white blood cell count and elevated protein
Normal white blood cell count with elevated protein

question: A 50-year-old man is brought to the hospital after being found confused and sweaty. His daughter, who has type 1 diabetes mellitus, finds him in the living room. His blood glucose on arrival is 35 mg/dL. Laboratory studies show an elevated serum insulin level and a suppressed C-peptide level. Which of the following is the most likely cause of his hypoglycemia?

A 26-year-old pregnant woman with a history of epilepsy is being managed with sodium valproate. She is concerned about the potential effects of the medication on her developing fetus. Prenatal screening at 18 weeks gestation reveals an elevated alpha-fetoprotein level. Which of the following fetal malformations is most closely associated with the use of this medication during pregnancy?

answers.option: Clear cell adenocarcinoma of the vagina

question: A 19-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department by her roommate 30 minutes after intentionally ingesting 20 tablets of 500 mg paracetamol. She is currently asymptomatic and her vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination is unremarkable. Which of the following is the most appropriate immediate step in the management of this patient?

A 45-year-old man with a history of poorly controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus presents with sudden-onset, severe epigastric pain radiating to his back, accompanied by nausea and vomiting. Physical examination reveals eruptive xanthomas on his extensor surfaces. Laboratory studies show a serum triglyceride level of 1,200 mg/dL. Which of the following conditions is most likely to be associated with this patient's lipid profile?

A 6-month-old boy is evaluated for abdominal distension and failure to thrive. Physical examination reveals significant hepatomegaly. Laboratory studies demonstrate hypoglycemia and hyperlactatemia. The patient is diagnosed with von Gierke disease. Which of the following is the most common mode of inheritance for this group of metabolic disorders?

A 24-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with acute shortness of breath and lightheadedness following a panic attack. She has no significant past medical history. Physical examination reveals a respiratory rate of 30/min. An arterial blood gas analysis shows the following: pH 7.59, PaCO₂​ 25 mmHg, PaO₂​ 94 mm Hg, and HCO₃⁻​ 22 mEq/L. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 28-year-old woman is planning a three-week relief mission to a region in sub-Saharan Africa where Plasmodium falciparum is endemic and known to be resistant to chloroquine. She has no significant medical history and is not pregnant. Which of the following is the most appropriate regimen for malaria prophylaxis in this patient?

A 28-year-old man presents to the emergency department with a two-day history of coughing up blood and decreased urine output. Physical examination reveals bilateral pulmonary crackles. Laboratory studies show an elevated serum creatinine level and hematuria with red blood cell casts. A kidney biopsy is performed, demonstrating linear deposits of immunoglobulins along the glomerular basement membrane on immunofluorescence. Which of the following is the most likely underlying cause of this patient's condition?

answers.option: Antibodies against the alpha-3 chain of type IV collagen

question: A 50-year-old man is brought to the clinic after three days of severe vomiting and diarrhea. He appears lethargic and has dry mucous membranes. His blood pressure is 95/60 mm Hg and his heart rate is 110/min. Laboratory evaluation reveals a blood urea nitrogen to creatinine ratio of 40:1 and a fractional excretion of sodium (FENa) of less than 1%. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient's renal abnormality?

A 35-year-old man presents with a single, well-demarcated, hypopigmented patch on his left forearm. He notes a complete loss of sensation within the lesion. Physical examination reveals a palpably thickened ulnar nerve on the same side. A skin biopsy shows granulomatous inflammation with very few acid-fast bacilli. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 22-year-old woman presents with concerns regarding excessive hair growth on her chin and upper lip, along with irregular menstrual cycles occurring every 45 to 60 days. Physical examination reveals a body mass index of 31 kg/m² and moderate acne. Laboratory studies show an elevated total testosterone level and an increased luteinizing hormone to follicle-stimulating hormone ratio. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 62-year-old man presents with massive splenomegaly and pancytopenia. He denies any lymphadenopathy. A peripheral blood smear is performed, revealing medium-sized lymphocytes with prominent cytoplasmic projections. These cells stain positive for tartrate-resistant acid phosphatase. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 5-year-old boy is brought to the pediatrician for recurrent ear infections and easy bruising over the past month. Physical examination reveals generalized cervical lymphadenopathy and significant hepatosplenomegaly. Laboratory studies show a white blood cell count of 50,000/mm³ with 80% blasts. Immunophenotyping shows the blasts are terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase positive. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 40-year-old man who recently emigrated from a tropical region is diagnosed with a Strongyloides stercoralis infection after larvae were identified in a stool sample. He reports intermittent abdominal pain and a pruritic, linear rash on his buttocks. Which of the following is the most appropriate first-line pharmacologic treatment for this patient?

A 27-year-old woman with immune thrombocytopenia has a persistent platelet count of 15,000/mm³ despite six weeks of high-dose corticosteroid therapy. She continues to experience frequent epistaxis and heavy menstrual bleeding. Which of the following is generally considered the next most appropriate step for definitive long-term management in steroid-refractory cases?

A 4-year-old boy is brought to a rural health clinic with reports of difficulty seeing in low-light environments. Physical examination of the eyes reveals dry, thickened conjunctiva and the presence of small, foamy, triangular-shaped white plaques on the bulbar conjunctiva. Which of the following is the most likely early clinical finding in this patient?

A 45-year-old man presents with a deepening voice, enlarging hands, and a persistent frontal headache. Physical examination reveals a prominent supraorbital ridge and a widened gap between his lower teeth. Visual field testing demonstrates bitemporal hemianopsia. Laboratory evaluation shows a significantly elevated insulin-like growth factor 1 level. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 32-year-old woman presents with generalized weakness, a sore tongue, and tingling in her hands and feet. She mentions having recurrent oral ulcers and following a strict vegan diet for several years. Laboratory studies show a hemoglobin level of 8.5 g/dL and a markedly elevated lactate dehydrogenase level of 790 U/L. Which of the following is most likely to be seen on a peripheral blood smear?

A 28-year-old woman presents to the emergency department for the fourth time in two months complaining of sudden-onset chest pain, abdominal discomfort, and a sense of impending doom. On each occasion, she is found to be tachypneic and tachycardic, but multiple electrocardiograms and cardiac enzyme tests have been normal. She continues to request further cardiac testing. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 30-year-old man recently diagnosed with human immunodeficiency virus infection presents for a preventive health visit. His CD4+ T-lymphocyte count is 450/mm³. He is interested in receiving vaccinations to prevent opportunistic or co-infections. Which of the following vaccines is routinely recommended for this patient?

A 26-year-old woman at 10 weeks gestation presents with palpitations, heat intolerance, and a tremor. Laboratory studies confirm a low thyroid-stimulating hormone level and an elevated free thyroxine level. A diagnosis of Graves disease is made. Which of the following medications is considered the safest first-line treatment during the first trimester of pregnancy?

A 35-year-old man presents with progressive weakness in his right hand following a road traffic accident. Physical examination reveals atrophy of the hypothenar eminence and loss of sensation over the little finger and the ulnar half of the ring finger. He is unable to adduct his thumb against resistance (positive Froment sign). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

answers.option: Radial nerve injury at the spiral groove
Median nerve damage at the carpal tunnel

question: A 68-year-old woman is found to have an incidental elevation in total serum protein during a routine check-up. Serum protein electrophoresis reveals a small monoclonal protein (M-protein) spike of 1.5 g/dL. She denies bone pain, fatigue, or weight loss. A bone marrow biopsy is performed and shows 4% plasma cells. Her calcium, creatinine, and hemoglobin levels are all within normal limits. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old woman with metastatic breast cancer to the bone is brought to the emergency department with confusion, constipation, and generalized weakness. Laboratory studies reveal a serum calcium level of 14.2 mg/dL. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial step in the management of this patient?

A 34-year-old woman presents with a sudden onset of weakness in both legs and a loss of sensation below the level of the umbilicus. She also reports urinary urgency. A magnetic resonance imaging scan of the spine reveals a hyperintense, enhancing lesion extending from the T6 to T8 segments. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A patient diagnosed with acute transverse myelitis at the thoracic level initially presents with flaccid paralysis, absent deep tendon reflexes, and loss of bladder tone below the level of the lesion. This clinical state, which precedes the later development of upper motor neuron signs like spasticity, is best described by which of the following?

A 28-year-old woman presents with drooping of her eyelids and difficulty climbing stairs that worsens throughout the day. Physical examination reveals bilateral ptosis and proximal muscle weakness in the upper and lower extremities. Her deep tendon reflexes and sensory examination are normal. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 22-year-old man undergoes screening for human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) as part of a routine health check. The initial fourth-generation HIV-1/2 antigen-antibody immunoassay is reactive. According to the standard diagnostic algorithm, which of the following is used to confirm the diagnosis?

answers.option: Polymerase chain reaction for viral load

question: A 40-year-old traveler returns from an endemic region with high-grade fever, impaired consciousness, and generalized seizures. A peripheral blood smear reveals a high parasite density of Plasmodium falciparum. Which of the following is the most appropriate first-line treatment for this patient?

A 60-year-old man with end-stage renal disease presents with palpitations. An electrocardiogram reveals a prolonged QT interval and peaked T waves. Laboratory studies show a serum potassium level of 7.2 mEq/L. Which of the following is the most appropriate immediate step to protect the patient from cardiac arrhythmias?

A 30-year-old man is found down after a crush injury. Laboratory evaluation reveals a blood urea nitrogen of 200 mg/dL, creatinine of 5.4 mg/dL, potassium of 7.0 mEq/L, and a serum calcium of 6.5 mg/dL. His creatine kinase level is 20,480 U/L. Which of the following is the most appropriate immediate management for his metabolic derangements?

A 45-year-old man who recently underwent transsphenoidal surgery for a pituitary tumor presents for a follow-up visit. He reports low libido and persistent fatigue. Laboratory evaluation shows a follicle-stimulating hormone level of 0.8 mIU/mL, a luteinizing hormone level of 0.6 mIU/mL, and an 8 a.m. cortisol level of 10 µg/dL. His prolactin level is 18 ng/mL. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

An 82-year-old woman is brought to the hospital by her family due to three days of confusion and decreased oral intake following a urinary tract infection. On examination, she is hypotensive and has dry mucous membranes. Laboratory studies reveal a significantly deranged creatinine level. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial management step?

A 28-year-old man presents with a painless ulcer on his penis. He also reports a generalized maculopapular rash involving the palms and soles. To confirm a diagnosis of syphilis in a patient with these symptoms, which of the following is considered the most specific treponemal test?

A 26-year-old man presents with an acute onset of generalized muscle weakness after attending a wedding feast the previous evening. He reports having had two similar episodes in the past year, both of which resolved within 24 hours. Physical examination reveals decreased deep tendon reflexes and symmetric 3/5 strength in all extremities. Laboratory evaluation during the episode shows a serum potassium level of 2.2 mEq/L. Which of the following is the most likely trigger for this patient's condition?

A 24-year-old man presents with a two-day history of a swollen, painful right knee and a low-grade fever. He also reports a three-day history of purulent urethral discharge. On examination, the knee is erythematous and tender, with a significant effusion. Synovial fluid analysis reveals a leukocyte count of 60,000/mm³ with 90% neutrophils and no crystals. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 72-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department with a high-grade fever, headache, and altered mental status. Physical examination reveals nuchal rigidity. A lumbar puncture is performed, and cerebrospinal fluid analysis shows a leukocyte count of 1,200/mm³ with a predominance of polymorphonuclear neutrophils, a low glucose level, and an elevated protein level. Which of the following pathogens is a common cause of bacterial meningitis in this age group?

A 55-year-old woman presents with a new-onset skin rash and fever. Two weeks ago, she started taking high-dose ibuprofen for chronic back pain. Laboratory evaluation reveals a serum creatinine of 2.1 mg/dL. Urinalysis shows white blood cell casts, red blood cells, and eosinophiluria. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 42-year-old man presents to the clinic for a routine physical examination. His blood pressure is 170/100 mm Hg. Urinalysis reveals 2+ protein and the presence of red blood cell casts. He also notes mild swelling around his eyes in the mornings. Which of the following is the most likely clinical syndrome in this patient?

A 50-year-old man presents with fatigue and early satiety. Physical examination reveals significant splenomegaly. A complete blood count shows a total leukocyte count of 150,000/mm³ with an increase in myelocytes, metamyelocytes, and band forms. Cytogenetic analysis confirms the presence of the Philadelphia chromosome, t(9;22). Which of the following is the most appropriate first-line treatment for this patient?

A 22-year-old man presents with high-grade fever and is prescribed a course of nitrofurantoin for a urinary tract infection. Two days later, he returns with yellowing of the sclera and dark-colored urine. On examination, he has mild hepatosplenomegaly. Laboratory evaluation reveals a decrease in hemoglobin and elevated indirect bilirubin. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step to confirm the underlying diagnosis?

A 23-year-old male presents to the clinic with a complaint of fever and dysuria for five days. He also reports pain in the right knee joint. His history is significant for having multiple sexual partners. His vitals are a heart rate of 112/min, respiratory rate of 16/min, blood pressure of 110/75 mm Hg, and temperature of 102°F. On examination, the right knee joint is swollen and tender to touch. Complete blood count reveals an increased total leukocyte count with predominant neutrophilia. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

answers.option: Septic arthritis due to Staphylococcus aureus

question: A 64-year-old man with type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and stage 3 chronic kidney disease presents for a follow-up visit. His most recent laboratory results show a serum creatinine of 2.5 mg/dL and a calculated glomerular filtration rate of 28 mL/min/1.73 m2. Which of the following medications should be discontinued to reduce the risk of lactic acidosis?

A 58-year-old man with chronic liver disease secondary to hepatitis C virus infection presents with increasing abdominal girth and pedal edema. Physical examination reveals shifting dullness and jaundice. Laboratory evaluation shows a serum sodium level of 128 mEq/L. Which of the following best describes the cause of this patient's sodium levels?

A 30-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department after being found unresponsive at home with an empty bottle of diazepam nearby. Her respiratory rate is 8/min and she is minimally responsive to painful stimuli. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial pharmacologic reversal agent for this patient?

A 55-year-old man with type 2 diabetes mellitus and chronic heart failure is started on empagliflozin. This medication is known to reduce the risk of hospitalization for heart failure and slow the progression of kidney disease. To which of the following classes of drugs does empagliflozin belong?

A 28-year-old woman at 24 weeks gestation presents with a persistent, severe headache and intermittent blurred vision for the past four days. Physical examination reveals bilateral papilledema. A magnetic resonance imaging scan of the brain does not show any space-occupying lesions or hydrocephalus. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step to evaluate for cerebral venous sinus thrombosis?

A 45-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department with the "worst headache of her life" followed by a brief loss of consciousness. On examination, she has nuchal rigidity and a positive Brudzinski sign. Laboratory studies reveal a serum sodium level of 128 mEq/L. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient's clinical presentation?

A 5-year-old boy is brought to the clinic with generalized edema and anasarca. Urinalysis reveals 4+ protein and no red blood cells. Light microscopy of a kidney biopsy specimen appears normal. However, electron microscopy demonstrates diffuse effacement of the podocyte foot processes. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 68-year-old man presents with a sudden loss of motor function in his right arm and right-sided facial drooping. On examination, he has a right-sided facial nerve palsy consistent with a cortical lesion. Strength is 2/5 in the right upper limb and 4/5 in the right lower limb. Which of the following arteries is most likely affected?

A 19-year-old woman presents to the office with complaints of low mood and decreased energy for the past two months. Her family reports that she has become socially withdrawn and no longer enjoys spending time with friends. She has also experienced significant weight loss and a decreased appetite. The patient states that she is unwilling to take any pharmacological treatments. Which of the following is the best initial treatment option for her?

A 65-year-old hypertensive man presents with a resting tremor in his right hand. He also demonstrates a tremor when his hand is extended. Physical examination reveals lead-pipe rigidity and bradykinesia on the right side of his body. His gait is characterized by short, shuffling steps and a lack of arm swing. Which of the following is the most likely clinical diagnosis?

A 30-year-old woman presents with fatigue and pica. Laboratory studies show a hemoglobin level of 10.2 g/dL and a mean corpuscular volume of 72 fL. A peripheral blood smear shows microcytic, hypochromic red blood cells. Which of the following is the most accurate laboratory test to confirm a diagnosis of iron deficiency anemia?

A 72-year-old man with a long history of resting tremors, rigidity, and postural instability passes away from pneumonia. An autopsy is performed to examine the brain tissue. Which of the following histopathological findings is most characteristic of his underlying neurological condition?

answers.option: Loss of pigmented neurons in the substantia nigra and presence of Lewy bodies
Spongiform changes in the cerebral cortex

question: A 10-year-old boy living in a rural, arid region presents with a painless, dark, crusted ulcer on his foot that has been present for three weeks. He has no systemic symptoms. A skin scraping from the edge of the ulcer shows amastigotes within macrophages. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 14-year-old boy presents with jaundice and right upper quadrant pain. An ultrasound reveals pigment gallstones. Laboratory studies show an increased mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration and a negative direct Coombs test. A peripheral blood smear reveals numerous small, round red blood cells lacking central pallor. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 34-year-old woman with Graves disease has been taking methimazole for the past two months. She presents to the clinic with a high-grade fever, a severe sore throat, and painful mouth ulcers. Physical examination reveals an erythematous pharynx without exudates. Laboratory evaluation shows a total white blood cell count of 1,200/mm³ and an absolute neutrophil count of 100/mm³. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient's condition?

A 38-year-old woman presents with a painful lump in the front of her neck that developed over the past week. She notes that the pain radiates to her jaw and ears. She also reports palpitations and heat intolerance. Her symptoms were preceded by a viral upper respiratory tract infection two weeks ago. Laboratory studies show an elevated free thyroxine level and a suppressed thyroid-stimulating hormone level. A radioactive iodine uptake scan shows a significantly decreased uptake of 2%. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 52-year-old woman presents with persistent itching after taking a hot shower and a feeling of fullness in her left upper abdomen. Physical examination reveals splenomegaly. Laboratory evaluation shows a hemoglobin level of 18.5 g/dL, a hematocrit of 56%, and a platelet count of 600,000/mm³. A mutation in the Janus kinase 2 (JAK2) gene is identified. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 28-year-old man presents with a painless, rubbery, non-tender lymph node in his left supraclavicular area that has been increasing in size for one month. He also reports drenching night sweats and a 5-kilogram weight loss. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step to establish a definitive diagnosis?

answers.option: Complete blood count with peripheral smear

question: A 60-year-old man with a 15-year history of type 2 diabetes mellitus undergoes a routine funduscopic examination. The ophthalmologist notes the presence of microaneurysms and dot-and-blot hemorrhages. Which of the following findings, if present, would most specifically indicate a progression to the "severe" stage of non-proliferative diabetic retinopathy?

answers.option: Venous beading in two or more quadrants

question: A 42-year-old male presents to the office with a complaint of decreased urinary output for the past three days and a maculopapular rash on his torso. He reports taking nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs frequently for joint pain. Laboratory evaluation reveals a serum creatinine of 2.4 mg/dL. Urinalysis reveals proteinuria, red blood cells, white blood cell casts, and eosinophiluria. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 23-year-old man is brought to the clinic by his family because he has been singing, screaming, and talking excessively for the past week. He has slept only two hours per night and claims he is currently designing a spacecraft for a secret mission. His family notes that three years ago, he had a four-month period where he could not leave his bed due to overwhelming sadness and lack of energy. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

answers.option: Major depressive disorder with psychotic features

question: A 35-year-old man with type 2 diabetes mellitus presents to the emergency department with abdominal pain, vomiting, and deep, rapid breathing. Physical examination reveals signs of severe dehydration. Laboratory studies show a serum glucose of 450 mg/dL, a serum bicarbonate of 14 mEq/L, and a serum sodium of 130 mEq/L. Urinalysis is positive for 3+ ketones. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old man presents with a loss of libido, erectile dysfunction, and generalized fatigue. He also reports feeling cold all the time and having dry skin. Laboratory evaluation shows a low serum testosterone, a low follicle-stimulating hormone, a low free thyroxine, and a low 8 a.m. cortisol level. Which of the following terms best describes the clinical state resulting from the deficiency of multiple anterior pituitary hormones?
Which of the following is the drug of choice for the treatment of acute mania?

A 17-year-old was brought to the emergency room after he went through a road traffic accident. The trauma surgeon had to perform an emergency splenectomy on the boy to save him. Which of the following would be the most appropriate time to vaccinate him?

A 60-year-old lady presented in the emergency room (ER) with a urinary tract infection (UTI) and confusion. She has not eaten or had anything to drink for 3 days. On examination, her blood pressure was 70/50 (very low). Which of the following fluids should be administered in this case?

A young female came to the outpatient department (OPD) with complaints of high-grade fever and burning micturition for 1 month. She has a history of therapeutic abortion about 6 weeks ago at a local health clinic. On examination, her blood pressure is 170/90 and a large mass is palpable in the hypochondrium extending up to the umbilicus. Her labs revealed increased total leukocyte count (TLC), urea, and creatinine. What is the most likely cause?

answers.option: Obstruction at level of ureter or renal pelvis

question: A 65-year-old woman came to the clinic. She has been on oral steroids for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and had a DEXA scan showing a T score of -1.8. Which of the following would be the best management?

A 45-year-old male patient, who is a known smoker, presents in the clinic with complaints of shortness of breath for 1 month. For the last 1 day, his shortness of breath has become severe. On examination, he has bilateral crepts up to the middle of the lungs. What will be the next best management step?

answers.option: IV furesomide to treat pulmonary edema

question:
A young patient presents with a history of fever for the last few days. On examination, his temperature is 104°F, his blood pressure (BP) is 100/50 and he appears dehydrated. On investigation, his hemoglobin was 11.4 g/dl, WBC: 5.2 × 109/L, and platelets 245,000 cells/mm3. Dengue NS1 antigen and IgM were negative. MP ICT was negative and blood culture showed no growth. 
What will be the management?
Which anti-tuberculosis drug has the bacteriostatic mechanism of action?
A man was asked to have screening done for HIV before starting a job. What will be the best test to confirm the diagnosis?
What is the most specific treatment for benzodiazepine overdose?

A middle-aged female with bipolar disorder was on lithium therapy. She accidentally took more than the intended dose. She has now presented in the ER with confusion, nausea, and vomiting. Her serum lithium value is 3.0 mEq/L (normal range is 0.6 to 1.2 mEq/L). What will be the next best management?
A young woman presented in the emergency department (ER) after suicidal salicylate ingestion. Her serum salicylic acid level was 734 mg/L. What will be the best management option for her?

A patient with a known case of renal artery stenosis presented to the physician with complaints of raised blood pressure. He was prescribed an anti-hypertensive drug but his hypertension worsened after a week. Which anti-hypertensive drug is responsible for this?
A patient was prescribed an angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitor and his creatinine has worsened. What is the most likely underlying cause?

A middle-aged man is known for hypertension, diabetes, and congestive heart failure. He has performed Umrah recently and has a history of infection. He experienced shortness of breath and was admitted to the CCU. Which inotropic agent should be given?
A young lady claims that a surgeon is in love with her. Her mother complains that she has tried visiting the surgeon multiple times. What type of delusion does she have?

A middle-aged farmer is brought to the physician by his son with a complaint of not eating, drinking water, and fear of going out due to the breeze. He is also salivating excessively. What is the most likely cause?
A young boy with a known case of Duchenne muscular dystrophy presented to the physician. What is the mode of inheritance of this disease?
Empagliflozin belongs to which class of drugs?
A patient presented in the emergency department (ER) with diabetic ketoacidosis. What is the immediate investigation performed for the management?
Which of the following is true about anticholinergic syndrome?
A middle-aged man presented to the physician with complaints of right-hand incoordination while driving. On examination, he has slurred speech and ataxia. Which region is most likely affected?

A young female presented in the emergency department with acetaminophen overdose with suicidal intent. Her INR was 3.2, a liver function test (AST and ALT) in the range of 6000 U/L, and Bilirubin 20 mg/dl. What is the best treatment option in this case?

A patient presented with weakness, lethargy, and significant weight loss of 5kg. His laboratory investigations revealed hypocalcemia and hyponatremia. What is the best investigation to reach the diagnosis?

A child presented in the outpatient department for a follow-up of his CBC report. His reports are as follows: hemoglobin = 4 g/dL, MCV = 49 fl. TLC and platelets were within the normal range. What is the next best investigation?

A 31-year-old male presented to the outpatient department (OPD) with complaints of jaundice. On taking a detailed history it was found he is on anti-malarial drugs. What is the most likely cause of this condition?
What is the treatment option for typhoid carriers?
A middle-aged patient who has a known case of hypertension and diabetes had a stroke and developed nystagmus. What is the most likely site of lesion?
A patient who is an alcoholic came to the physician with complaints of forgetfulness, he does not remember the names of his family members. What is the term for this condition?
What is the treatment of cholinergic crisis?
What is the prognostic marker for systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE)?

A 30-year-old pregnant woman, who is a known case of Grave's disease and has been taking medications for it came for consultation regarding her treatment during pregnancy. Which of the following will be the drug of choice for this patient?
What is the treatment for oligomenorrhea?
A 70-year-old man with a history of memory loss for 6 years. He has now started to behave aggressively towards his family and gets lost. What is the management of Alzheimer's disease?
What is the best treatment for the case of organophosphate poisoning?
A 30-year-old patient presents with complaints of 5 kg weight loss, fatigue, lethargy, polyuria, and polydipsia. His blood sugar level was raised. What is the best treatment for this patient?
A 30-year-old male came to the outpatient department with complaints of ulcers on his penis. On examination, he has rashes on his palms and soles. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A young female presents to her gynecologist complaining of irregular menstrual periods, galactorrhea, and decreased libido. She also reports experiencing headaches and vision changes (visual field defects). Physical examination reveals no abnormalities. A blood test is performed and prolactin levels are 800 ng/mL. What is the best management for this patient?
What are the lab findings in hypopituitarism?

A woman presented to the clinic with her husband with complaints of amenorrhea for 4 months. The couple has 2 kids and the husband has azoospermia. The woman has prolactin levels of 400 ng/ml. What will be the next best step?
What is the most sensitive and specific test for syphilis?
What is the best test for disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC)?
A patient presented in the emergency department (ER) with Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA). His serum sodium levels were 106 mmol/L. Which of the following fluids would be administered?

A 60-year-old lady with NKCM presented in the outpatient department (OPD) with complaints of dyspnea and stridor. Examination revealed a large retrosternal goiter. Her thyroid profile was normal. Which of the following would be the best management?

A 65-year-old man, with a known case of COPD presented in the clinic with complaints of fever, confusion, and dyspnea. On examination, his Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) was 12/15 and there was dullness to percussion at the left lower lung. 
His lab values revealed hyponatremia, normal K+ levels, and increased TLC. He was given 3% saline and his GCS improved. What was likely the cause of his hyponatremia?

A middle-aged man with a known case of lung cancer presented in the clinic with complaints of muscle weakness that improves with activity. He also complains of dry mouth. On examination, his DTR was absent. What is the most likely diagnosis?
In which of the following diseases the dose of levothyroxine is reduced?
A child presented in the clinic with abdominal pain. His serum complement levels were normal. What is the most likely cause?
Which of the following is the side effect of cyclophosphamide drug?
Which of the following is true regarding De Quervain thyroiditis?

answers.option: Anti-thyroid drugs are effective in treatment

question:
A 60-year-old lady presented in the clinic with complaints of irritability and lethargy. Her lab values showed Ca=11.2 mg/dL, phosphate levels were low and ALP was raised.
What is the best next step to reach the diagnosis?
Which of these is a universal screening tool for dementia?
Which of these anti-retroviral drugs is a classic cause of lipodystrophy?

A 21-year-old female patient with a history of epilepsy presents to the emergency department with a seizure lasting for more than 30 minutes. Despite the administration of diazepam and phenytoin, the patient's seizure activity continues. What is the next best step in management?

A 60-year-old patient with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia presents with fatigue, weight loss, and night sweats.
