Further evaluation reveals a high white blood cell count and splenomegaly. A diagnosis of myeloproliferative disorder is made. What is the drug of choice for the management of this condition?
What is the first-line treatment option for immune thrombocytopenic purpura?

A 19-year-old male presents to the office with complaints of low mood and decreased energy for the past 2 months. His family says he does not like going out with his friends anymore, while he used to be always outgoing. He has also had significant weight loss and decreased appetite. The patient says he does not wanna take any drugs. What is the best treatment option for him?

A 24-year-old male presents to the emergency with a new-onset blurring of vision with mild drooping of the eyelid. He reports being bitten by a snake in his village a few hours ago for which he only used a tourniquet and sucked out the venom. Which snakebite can lead to such a presentation?

A 19-year-old woman presents to the office with the complaint of a painful rash over her genitals for the last 2 days. She has multiple sexual partners. On physical examination, there are multiple ulcerated lesions over both her labia along with tender inguinal lymphadenopathy. What is the most likely organism responsible for her presentation?
Which one of these is the single best test for the diagnosis of polycythemia vera?

A 25-year-old female presents to the clinic with symptoms of lower abdominal pain and a yellow-green discharge from her cervix. She reports having unprotected sexual contact with a new partner. Gram staining of her discharge reveals gram-negative intracellular diplococci. Which of these organisms is most likely responsible for her symptoms?

A 34-year-old woman presents to the office after a positive pregnancy test. Her last pregnancy was 8 years ago, which was a miscarriage. She is diagnosed case of APLA syndrome. Which of these is the best management option for her current pregnancy?

A 33-year-old male presents to the emergency with the complaint of palpitations for the last few hours. Arrival EKG reveals atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular rate. IV esmolol is administered and the patient achieves a normal heart rate. The hemodynamics are stable, and a transesophageal echocardiogram reveals no thrombus in the left atrium. Which of these is the next best step in management?
Which one of these kidney pathologies is characterized by tram-track appearance?

An 8-year-old male presents to the clinic with a history of recurrent episodes of abdominal pain, joint pain, and skin rashes. He also reports frequent episodes of fever and blood in the urine. The patient's mother says that these symptoms have been occurring for several months and have been getting worse over time.

Upon examination, the patient is found to have joint pain and stiffness in his knees, ankles, and wrists. He also has a diffuse, non-pruritic rash on his lower legs and feet. The patient's abdomen is mildly tender to palpation, and he has difficulty standing and walking due to pain and stiffness in his joints. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old man presents to the emergency department with a 2-week history of fatigue, weakness, and weight loss. He also complains of nausea, vomiting, and dizziness. He has a history of chronic corticosteroid use for rheumatoid arthritis. On examination, he is hypotensive and has hyperpigmentation of the skin. His laboratory results show low sodium, glucose, and high potassium levels. Serum cortisol is low. What is the next best step in management?

A 25-year-old male presents to the office with progressive difficulty in walking which started when he was 12. He has had a long history of associated falls and is now wheelchair-bound. His family history is positive for a similar disorder in his grand dad who eventually died of cardiac arrest. Examination findings reveal scoliosis of the spine. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 25-year-old man presents to the emergency department after being bitten by a snake while hiking. He reports severe pain and swelling at the site of the bite, as well as nausea, vomiting, and difficulty breathing. Physical examination reveals a puncture wound on his left ankle which is constantly oozing out blood, as well as significant edema and ecchymosis in the surrounding area. The patient's blood pressure is low and his heart rate is elevated. Lab counts reveal thrombocytopenia. What is the management of choice for this patient?

A 23-year-old male presents to the office with complaints of fever and a painful mass in front of his neck for the last couple of days. He reports having a flu-like illness a week back. On examination, the mass is tender and moves on deglutition. Laboratory investigations reveal an increased ESR. What is the management for this patient?

A 32-year-old woman presents with complaints of weight loss and palpitations for the past 3 months. She has no significant past medical history. Examination shows a midline neck swelling that moves on deglutition. If this patient is set to undergo radioisotope scanning, what is the most likely finding?

answers.option: Uptake in one nodule and diminished in other areas

question: A 27-year-old woman presents to the office with the complaint of inability to conceive for the past 12 months. She had one term child delivered 6 years ago. She has noticed that she has gained weight despite having a normal diet and that her menses have become irregular for the past 4 months. She has also started feeling fatigued throughout her day. What is the best initial investigation for her?
Which of these entities explain the following ABG values: pH=7.68, pCO2=22mmHg, and HCO3=25mEq/L?
A 35-year-old male is being investigated for a thyroid nodule. Ultrasound shows a hypoechoic nodule with microcalcifications. What is the next best step?

A 57-year-old male presents to his primary care physician with the chief complaint of increased size of his hands and feet, as well as a deepening of his voice over the past several years. He also reports experiencing excessive sweating, fatigue, and joint pain. Lab tests reveal an HbA1c of 7.3%. What is the single best initial investigation for this patient?

A 32-year-old female presents to her gynecologist complaining of irregular menstrual periods and decreased libido. She also reports experiencing headaches and vision changes. Physical examination reveals no abnormalities. A blood test is performed and prolactin levels are found to be 1000ng/mL. What is the best management for this patient?

A 35-year-old male patient presents to the clinic complaining of excessive sweating, fatigue, and joint pain. He also reports having a history of a growing jaw, forehead, and hands over the past few years. Physical examination reveals a tall and overweight patient with coarse facial features, thickened skin, and enlarged hands and feet. Further investigations are performed, including blood tests, which reveal elevated levels of calcium and parathyroid hormone (PTH). What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 24-year-old female patient presents to her primary care physician complaining of irregular menstrual cycles and difficulty getting pregnant. She also reports experiencing acne, hirsutism (excess hair growth), and weight gain. Lab investigations reveal elevated levels of androgens. Her BMI is 29. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 28-year-old female patient presents to her endocrinologist with a complaint of excessive hair growth on her face, chest, and back. She reports that this hair growth has been rapidly worsening over the past year and is causing her significant distress. Her voice has also changed over this last year. Lab investigations reveal elevated levels of DHEA-S. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 32-year-old male patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden onset of fever, headache, confusion, and seizures. The patient reports that he has been experiencing flu-like symptoms for the past few days but his condition has rapidly worsened. The patient has no known medical history and no known risk factors for encephalitis.

A CT scan of the patient's brain shows evidence of inflammation and damage in the temporal lobes. A lumbar puncture is performed, and the patient's cerebrospinal fluid reveals a high RBC and lymphocyte count, and mildly elevated protein levels. In addition to antiepileptic therapy, which other drug needs to be administered in this case?

A 60-year-old man is treated with a typical antipsychotic medication for psychosis. After a few months of treatment, the patient starts to experience symptoms such as tremors, stiffness and slowing of movements. What is the most likely diagnosis?
What is the investigation of choice for Von Willebrand disease?

A 35-year-old male with a history of myasthenia gravis presents to the emergency department with severe muscle weakness, difficulty speaking and breathing, and excessive salivation. He reports that he had recently increased his dosage of pyridostigmine, a medication used to treat myasthenia gravis because his symptoms had been worsening. He also reports that he has been experiencing abdominal cramps and diarrhea. On physical examination, the patient is visibly fatigued, with a weak and flaccid muscle tone. What is the most likely diagnosis?
What is the initial fluid of choice in the management of diabetic ketoacidosis?
What is the initial treatment of choice in hyperosmolar hyperglycemic syndrome (HHS)?
What is the management of choice in a kid with a positive Mantoux test but negative CXR for tuberculosis?
Which one of these organisms characteristically causes anemia with high MCV (110)?

A patient with a history of Type 1 diabetes presents to the emergency department with a blood sugar level of 600 mg/dL and a pH of 7.1. The patient has been experiencing profuse vomiting for 24 hours and is showing signs of dehydration. The patient's potassium level is found to be 2.2 mEq/L. What is the most likely cause of the patient's hypokalemia in this scenario?

An 18-year-old girl presents with profuse vomiting and diarrhea for the past 12 hours. She is drowsy, and lab values reveal a Na level of 124 mEq/L. Physical examination shows signs of dehydration. What is the best initial management for this patient?

A 6-year-old child presents to the clinic with complaints of peri-orbital puffiness for the past 3 months. Urine analysis shows proteinuria. A trial of steroid therapy is given and an excellent response is achieved. What is the characteristic microscopic finding in this patient?

A 75-year-old woman presents with a history of forgetfulness and disorientation. She has trouble remembering names and recent events and often gets lost in familiar places. She has also become increasingly confused and agitated, especially at night. The patient's husband reports that she has trouble completing simple tasks and making decisions. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old woman presents with fatigue, muscle weakness, and a history of recurrent kidney stones. Her lab results show elevated serum calcium levels and decreased serum phosphorus levels. What is the most likely diagnosis?
Which one of these is not a feature of prerenal AKI?

A 42-year-old male presents to the office with the complaint of decreased urinary output for the past 3 days. He reports taking NSAIDs from time to time for pain relief for his joint pain. Urine testing reveals proteinuria and an intrinsic renal injury pattern, with RBC and eosinophilic casts. What is the most likely diagnosis?
Which one of these is the single best test for the diagnosis of enteric fever?
What is the drug of choice for amebic liver abscesses?
A 44-year-old woman presents with the complaint of perianal itching, especially at night. Infection by Enterobius vermicularis is suspected. What diagnostic test can be used for it?
What is the best treatment regimen for Hodgkin lymphoma?
Which of these sleeping pills are least likely to cause a hangover?

A 55-year-old male with a history of HIV presents with a sudden onset of vision changes in his right eye. Physical exam reveals blurred vision and a pale retina with exudates and hemorrhages in the affected eye. The patient reports no other symptoms. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 65-year-old female presents with sudden onset of weakness on her right side, difficulty speaking, and confusion. On examination, there is sensory loss and paralysis of her right face, arm, and leg. Which vessel involvement is most likely responsible?
Which one of these drugs is to be 'added' in addition to the usual empiric regimen for meningitis in a 75-year-old male?

A 25-year-old man presents to the neurology outpatient clinic with complaints of weakness of all four limbs for the last 2 days. He had a diarrheal illness 2 weeks ago that resolved after taking antibiotics. On examination, his speech and higher mental functions are intact. He also has bilateral facial nerve palsy. Power in both upper and lower limb muscles was 3/5 with absent reflexes and mute plantars. Which of the following abnormalities would be expected in the nerve conduction studies at this time?

A 25-year-old pregnant woman is found to have microcytic anemia during her antenatal visits. Her Hb is 7 mg/dL with an MCV of 66 fL. Which of the following is the single best test for the confirmation of iron deficiency anemia?
A 57-year-old man presents with hypertrophy of gums and is diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML). Which of the following is characteristic of this condition?

A 54-year-old man presents with the complaint of progressive muscle weakness. Laboratory results show a potassium concentration of 7 mmol/L. ECG shows widening of QRS complexes. Which of the following is the first step in management?

A 30-year-old man is referred to the clinic for evaluation of visual field defects. Additional complaints include fatigue, myalgia, headache, bilateral knee pain, and excessive perspiration. His blood pressure is 156/94 mm Hg, pulse 56/ minute, weight 105 kg, and height 6 feet 2 inches. His hands are thick and enlarged; his calcaneus could not be felt through his heel pad. Laboratory studies are as follows: free thryoxine index 3.6 mcg/dL (4-11 mcg/dL), TSH 0.7 U/L, testosterone 87 ng/dL (300 - 1000 ng/dL), LH 3.2 mIU/mL (2 - 28 mIU/mL), prolactin 5 ng/dL (< 8 ng/dL), 8 am cortisol 2 mcg/dL (6-24 mcg/dL), and fasting glucose 186 mg/dL. Which of the following diagnoses best explains the patient's signs and symptoms?
A 28-year-old sexually active woman comes to the genitourinary clinic with multiple painful genital ulcers. Which of the following is the most likely causative organism?

A 28-year-old male nurse comes to the clinic for evaluation of tuberculosis. He had been in contact with patients having active pulmonary tuberculosis for the last 2 months. His Monteux test was 12 mm one month ago. Clinically, this person has no symptoms. Which of the following is the most important investigation to obtain at this time?

A 30-year-old woman is brought to the clinic by with complaints of abnormal movements of the face, memory impairment, and complex partial seizures for 2 months, Her neurological examination reveals a low MMSE score and orofacial dyskinesia. On systemic examination, a firm mass is palpated in the left iliac fossa. Her MRI brain shows high-intensity signals in the hippocampus. Cerebrospinal fluid analysis shows raised proteins. CT scan of the pelvis shows a left ovarian mass. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 30-year-old woman presents to the clinic with irritability of mood and over talkativeness for one week. She attends to her routine activities and there is no functional decline. In fact, she grooms herself overly and is meticulously concerned about her appearance. She has a past history of multiple depressive episodes. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 34-year-old woman presents to the clinic with pallor, jaundice, and splenomegaly. Her complete blood count shows Hb 9 g/dL and MCV 107 fL. Direct Coomb's test is positive. She is diagnosed with warm autoimmune hemolytic anemia and treated with steroids, but the patient does not respond. Which of the following is the next best step in management?

A 58-year-old man, who has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, presents to the clinic with worsening hypertension. On examination, he is anemic and has pedal edema. His blood pressure is 180/100 mm Hg. Which of the following investigations is the most specific for the function of the kidney?

A 60-year-old woman presents with a 4-month history of progressive lethargy and recurrent throat infections. Recently, she developed gum bleeding and noticed purpura all over her body. She is anemic, but the remainder of the examination is normal. Investigations show Hb 7 g/dL, white cell count 83000/uL, and platelets 18000/uL. Bone marrow biopsy shows hypercellular marrow with a decrease in normal precursor cells.; 85% of the cells are myeloblasts. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 42-year-old woman comes to the clinic for evaluation of uncontrolled blood sugar. She has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus and takes glimepiride 20 mg every day before breakfast. Her BMI is 32 kg/m2 and HbA1c is 8.4%. Which of the following is the best treatment option for this patient?

answers.option: Add on metformin and strictly follow life-style modification
Add an DPP-4 inhibitor and follow life-style modification
Add on thiazolidinone and strictly follow lifestyle modification

question: A 20-year-old man is referred to the diabetes clinic with newly diagnosed diabetes (fasting glucose on two occasions >289 mg/dL). He has had osmotic symptoms (polyuria and polydipsia) for 6 months, and his weight has recently increased by around 14 kg. On examination, there are purplish striae on the abdomen with central obesity. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 50-year-old man presents to the clinic with marked heaviness in the left hypochondrium. He has also had experienced early satiety for 3 months. On examination, the liver is enlarged, 3 cm below the costal margin amd the spleen is massively enlarged up to the umbilicus. Considering myelofibrosis as a diagnosis, which of the following is the only approved treatment?
A 16-year-old boy has type 1 diabetes mellitus and is on mixed insulin twice daily. His HbA1c is 9.5%. Which of the following is the best next step in management?

answers.option: Put him on basal bolus regimen
Put him on split dosage of insulin twice thrice daily
Increase the current dosage of insulin
Put him on sliding scale of insulin

question: A 24-year-old man presents to the clinic for evaluation of primary infertility. His semen analysis on two separate occasions shows severely abnormal spermatogenesis. Which of the following is the cause of this abnormality?

A 79-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with complaints of confusion, headache, and tinnitus. Her general practitioner has recently started her on an analgesic; the physician on duty is worried she may have taken too much. Which of the following would most likely explain her symptoms?

A 68-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a history of easy fatigability and back pain. On examination, she is anemic and has tender bones. Her initial investigations show Hb 9.8 g/dL, MCV 84 fl, platelets 141 x 10^3/L, creatinine 2.3 mg/dL, ALP 84 IU, and SGPT 32 IU. Bone scan shows lytic lesions. Which of the following is the next best step in diagnosis?

A young woman has a history of blood culture positive Salmonella typhi infection 3 months ago, for which she received complete therapy and recovered fully. While applying to a certain job, some routine investigations are done and it is found that she is shedding Salmonella bacilli in her stool. The physician labels her as a case of Salmonella carrier stage. Which of the following types of carrier stage is now present in this patient?

A 35-year-old man presents to the neurology clinic with complaints of progressive weakness of the right hand for the last 3 months. He had a road traffic accident around 3 and a half months back, in which he sustained multiple fractures. On examination, he has weakness of the small muscles of the hand and loss of sensation to pinprick over the medial palm, little finger, and medial half of the ring finger. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 40-year-old woman has a 15-year history of multiple sclerosis. She develops severe generalized spasticity and started on multiple oral anti-spasticity drugs. Rehabilitative measures also show poor response. Which of the following is the next best available treatment option for this woman?

A 20-year-old anxious-looking woman consults her physician with recurrent abdominal pain, bloating, and discomfort for the last 6 months. She also complains of altered bowel habits, predominantly diarrhea. Her abdominal pain improves after passing stool. There is no history of fever and weight loss. Physical examination is unremarkable. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 12-year-old boy is found in a closed room with increased salivation from the mouth and sweating profusely. His pulse is 50 beats/minute and blood pressure is 100/60 mm Hg. Which of the following is the most appropriate antidote?
In chronic renal failure, if the patient's plasma K+ levels are found to be 7.5 mmol/L, which of the following is the most appropriate initial step?
Which of the following is the most common infection presenting as pyrexia of unknown origin?
A 45-year-old woman with a history of high-grade fever is diagnosed with malaria due to Plasmodium vivax. Which of the following is the drug of choice?
In a patient with HIV, a chest X-ray shows bilateral interstitial infiltrates spreading out from the hilar region. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
Which of the following investigations is used for the definitive diagnosis of enteric fever?
Which of the following is not a cause of mononeuritis multiplex?

A 40-year-old female checked her own random blood glucose level using a glucometer in the mid-afternoon and it was 186 mg/dl (reference range <140). She is currently asymptomatic and reports no excessive urination or thirst. Her medical history is unremarkable. Her mother has a 15-year history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, with onset at age 49. On physical examination, the patient's height is 164 cm, weight is 73.5 kg, and BMI is 27.3. Her heart rate is 82 beats/minute and her blood pressure is 128/82 mmHg. Velvety hyperpigmentation is noted on the posterior folds of her neck. The next morning, the patient presents after 8 hours of fasting and laboratory testing yields the following result: fasting plasma glucose - 94 mg/dl, and plasma glucose 2 hours after an oral load of 75 gm of glucose - 177 mg/dl. Which of the following is the correct interpretation of this patient's blood test results?

answers.option: The patient can be considered to have a normal glucose profile; no additional testing is needed
Autoantibody testing is indicated before making a diagnosis
At least one of the tests should be repeated on another day before making a diagnosis
The patient can be diagnosed with impaired glucose tolerance; no additional testing is needed
The glucose tests should be repeated after 12 hours of fasting

question: A 25-year-old female is diagnosed with porphyria variegate. Which of the following may be included as part of the specific management of this condition?

answers.option: Avoidance of agents that can precipitate the condition
Intravenous glucose as provision of 55 KJ per day

question: A 36-year-old female presents to the clinic with complaints of secondary amenorrhea and headache for 6 months. She has 3 children, the last-born is 2 years old. She started oral contraceptives after the birth of her last born, but stopped 11 months ago. She has also noted weight gain during the same time period. On examination, Ferriman-Gallwey score is 8/32, secondary sexual characteristics are well developed and there is no galactorrhea. However, visual confrontation shows left inferior temporal field defects. Serum thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) is 2.4 (0.4-4.0), luteinizing hormone (LH) is 0.2 (1.2-4.0), follicular stimulating hormone (FSH) is 2.0 (2.0-8.0) and prolactin levels are 90 (10-23). What is the most likely cause of her presentation?

A 40-year-old male presents to the emergency department complaining of tiredness and muscular weakness. On investigation, his plasma potassium level is 2.4 mmol/L. Which of the following ECG change is most likely to occur in severe hypokalemia?

A 31-year-old female presents to the medical outpatient department with complaints of amenorrhea for the past six months along with dyspareunia and bone pain all over the body. Investigations reveal negative urine pregnancy test, high concentrations of luteinizing hormone (LH) and follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) along with low or low-normal estradiol. Which of the following is the most likely cause of amenorrhea in this patient?

A 40-year-old man presents with easy fatigability. Investigations reveal hemoglobin (Hb) - 9 g/dL, mean corpuscular volume (MCV) - 105 fL, and spherocytes on peripheral blood film. Which of the following is the most common abnormality in hereditary spherocytosis?

A 35-year-old woman presents to the clinic with complaints of lethargy, palpitations, and weakness. She has had a profound weight loss of 12 Kg over the last 4 months. On examination, there are tremors of the hands and sweaty palms. Her eyes have a constant stare and she looks very frightened. There is a diffuse, firm goiter that moves with deglutition. Her thyroid function tests are as follows: thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH) - <0.001 (0.4-4.0), total T4 - 20.9 (5.0-11.2), free T4 - 1.9 (0.86-1.76). Which of the following is the most likely cause of her condition?

A 45-year-old male presents to you with complaints of early satiety and heaviness for the past 2 months. He also gives history of blurring of vision and severe headache for the past week. His labs show hemoglobin - 10.1 mg/dL, white blood cells - 79,000/mm3, platelets - 950,000 and left myeloid shift on peripheral smear. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 10-year-old boy presents to you with a complaint of severe pain in his hands and feet. He is febrile, mildly jaundiced, and dehydrated. Labs show hemoglobin 0 5.6 gm/dL, reticulocyte count - 8%, total bilirubin - 2.5 mg, SGPT - 20. Family history is significant for a similar illness in his brother 1 year ago. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

answers.option: Sickle cell disease with vaso-occlusive crisis

question: Which of the following investigations is the best to diagnose multiple sclerosis, along with history and examination?

answers.option: CT scan of the brain with contrast
Magnetic resonance imaging of the brain

question: Which of the following is true regarding paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria (PNH)?

answers.option: Flow cytometry does not help in diagnosis
It does not progress to myelodysplasia or acute myeloid leukemia
It can be suspected in confusing cases of hemolytic anemia or pancytopenia

question: Which of the following is the most important indication for hospital admission in depressive patients?
